findings: The parsing, error handling, output, return-code rules, and examples define a satisfiable executable CLI contract.
All I/O behavior, exit codes, and error handling are precisely defined for every input, including empty and malformed files.
Examples are consistent with the general rules (e.g., overlapping ranges allowed, malformed lines reported and skipped, no-valid-range case returns 1).
The contract is executable and deterministic with no ambiguity or contradiction.
The replacement, trimming, uppercasing, and empty-input rules are deterministic and consistent with the examples.
Normalization rules (collapse spaces/tabs/dashes to underscore, trim underscores, uppercase) are fully specified and deterministic.
Behavioral examples match the stated transformation rules, including empty/whitespace-only inputs mapping to empty string.
No conflicting constraints or underdefined behavior remain.
Unicode whitespace is objectively defined through str.isspace(), and the validation and transformation rules are complete.
Whitespace definition is tied to str.isspace(), and replacement with single ASCII space plus stripping is fully specified.
Type checking and TypeError conditions are clearly defined; all inputs are covered deterministically.
Behavioral tests agree with the stated rules, and there is no internal contradiction.
Per-group integer summation, validation, ordering, and non-mutation requirements are mutually consistent and executable.
Input types and error conditions (non-list groups or non-int elements) are clearly defined and lead to TypeError with no partial output.
Sum semantics for each group, including empty lists and negatives, are fully specified and match examples.
The requirement that input is not modified is implementable and does not conflict with other constraints.
The accepted opening brackets, matching closing brackets, and one-pair removal behavior are explicitly defined and consistent with the examples.
Accepted bracket characters and their matching closers are explicitly listed; other brackets cause ValueError.
The rule for stripping exactly one leading opener and one trailing matching closer, otherwise leaving the string unchanged, is precise and deterministic.
All edge examples (nested brackets, only pair, empty string) are consistent with the general rule.
The group rotation algorithm, partial-group behavior, and invalid-input handling are objective and satisfiable.
Rotation is clearly defined groupwise with right-cyclic shift within each (possibly partial) group.
Type and value checks for group_size and for strings elements are precise (ValueError vs TypeError).
Examples align with the group rotation rule, and the contract is deterministic and executable with no ambiguity.
Strict and casefold adjacency semantics, mode validation, and type validation are explicitly specified and objectively testable.
The deduplication rule for 'strict' vs 'casefold' modes is fully specified and deterministic.
Type constraints for inputs and mode, and corresponding TypeError/ValueError conditions, are clear and cover all invalid inputs.
There is no ambiguity about behavior for any list of strings and allowed modes; the requirement is objectively checkable.
The empty-delimiter case is expressly defined: the entire phrase is returned as one trimmed uppercase token, so no material ambiguity remains.
Behavior for empty delimiter is explicitly defined: return the entire phrase as a single uppercase string, so no use of Python’s native split on empty delimiter is required.
Splitting behavior for nonempty delimiters, trimming whitespace, and uppercasing tokens are all fully specified and deterministic, including empty tokens from consecutive delimiters.
Type errors for phrases and delimiter types are clearly defined; there is no remaining under-specification preventing objective certification.

For input 'a, b,#ignore', the general rule requires reversing all three comma-separated fields with content preserved, while the required example omits the '#ignore' field and outputs only two fields.
Fields are clearly defined as segments between commas, and the requirement to preserve field content exactly (including spaces) makes handling of empty/whitespace-only fields unambiguous.
Lines with no commas but not empty/comment are explicitly malformed; error handling and exit codes are fully specified.
The claimed ambiguity about empty fields is resolved by the stated preservation rule, so the contract is executable and objectively testable.
For n=3, the contract requires all involutions but explicitly requires only [[0,1,2]]; permutations [0,2,1], [1,0,2], and [2,1,0] are also involutions.
The function domain is finite for each call (fixed n), and returning all involutive permutations is computationally large but mathematically well-defined and implementable for any given n.
Deterministic lexicographic ordering and edge-case examples are consistent with the definition of involutions.
No logical contradiction exists; unbounded growth in output size does not make the contract infeasible in principle.
The zero-occurrence condition simply yields [[]] when b=0 and [] when b>0; a valid empty result makes the contract satisfiable.
For a>0 and b>0, any b-length list with elements restricted to 0..a-1 must contain at least one such integer at least once, contradicting the requirement that each appear exactly zero times.
The requirement nonetheless demands returning all such lists for general a,b, leading to an empty feasible set for all a>0,b>0.
This is a direct logical contradiction in the constraints, so only trivial empty-length cases can satisfy, proving general infeasibility.
The reverse-pair condition can be applied as a filter over the finite bounded candidate pairs; inputs with no qualifying pairs validly return an empty list.

For any given a,b,total, the set of (x,y) with 0<=x<a,0<=y<b,x+y=total and x≠y is finite and well-defined; the extra requirement is simply to filter to those pairs whose reverse also satisfies the same constraints and include both.
Cases where no such symmetric pairs exist (e.g., a=2,b=2,total=1) are correctly handled by returning an empty list; this is not a contradiction but a valid outcome.
The contract does not require the existence of pairs for all parameters, only that all valid symmetric ones be returned without duplicates in deterministic order.
